question: In June 2022 the EU Gas Storage Regulation was introduced to meet the challenges posed by the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The regulation requires Member States to ‘take all necessary measures including providing financial incentives or compensation’ to ensure that companies that help to reach the EU’s storage targets do not suffer financially from doing so. Most Member States have honoured this requirement.

Bulgaria has yet to do so, leaving private operators in financial peril. The state-owned compagny Bulgargaz is benefiting from this failure to honour the requirement. Bulgargaz is part of a controversial deal with the Turkish state-owned company BOTAS, which is highly likely providing a back door for Russian gas to be funneled into EU networks. 1.
Why has the Commission not ensured that all Member States put in place working compensatory mechanisms as required by the 2022 EU Gas Storage Regulation?
What steps is the Commission taking to ensure that Bulgaria in particular meets its compensatory requirements?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.4.2024) The Gas Security of Supply Regulation (EU) 2017/1938, as amended by the Gas Storage Regulation1 in 2022, provides that Member States shall take all necessary measures to meet the filling target of 90% by 1 November each year.

According to the Regulation, Member States can adopt the measures listed in the Regulation in order to support storage filling, such as the ones providing for financial incentives or compensation to market participants. However, there is no obligation for Member States to adopt such measures.

Nevertheless, if and once adopted, the measures have to be limited to what is necessary to meet the filling trajectories and filling targets. They shall be clearly defined, transparent, proportionate, non-discriminatory and verifiable. They shall also not unduly distort competition or the proper functioning of the internal market in gas or endanger the security of gas supply of other Member States or of the Union.

As guardian of the Treaties, the Commission is carefully monitoring the situation in Bulgaria and in other Member States regarding the legality of any measures and may decide to take appropriate action if necessary.
